candidates.rationale: Uses StarDist 2D with checkpoint 2D_versatile_fluo, percentile normalization [1, 99.8], probability threshold 0.479071463157368, and NMS threshold 0.3. The user declares Hoechst-stained U2OS fluorescence; my visual observation is bright, mostly compact or elongated nucleus-like regions on a dark background, with some touching and border-truncated regions. The supplied probe reports replicated grayscale, which supports the channel requirement but does not establish modality. This is my preferred starting procedure because its fluorescence-nuclei checkpoint and star-convex representation suit much of the visible morphology, and its intermediate probability threshold avoids committing to either lower-threshold inclusion or higher-threshold rejection without evidence favoring either. This is not a demonstrated accuracy advantage. Star-convex assumptions and unfamiliar imaging scales remain limitations. No measurement evidence is supplied, so a numeric count cannot yet be returned.

Checkpoint suitability for this stain, magnification, and pixel size is unverified; no ground-truth labels or benchmark scores are available.

These flow-consistency and cell-probability controls are not equivalent to StarDist's probability and NMS thresholds. The minimum-size filter may remove small artifacts but could also remove small visible border fragments. No explicit preprocessing parameters are supplied, so equivalence to StarDist normalization should not be assumed. This offers an alternative segmentation approach, but its generalist output may merge touching nuclei or segment other structures and does not prove biological identity. The registered procedure requires Apple MPS and is limited here to 2D grayscale fluorescence nuclei; no comparative accuracy evidence favors it.
